finding.claim: The DELETE /projects/:id handler calls authorized(), which returns a boolean, but ignores the result. Any caller who reaches the route can delete any project. The sibling PUT route uses authorize(), which throws, so this looks like a mix-up of the two helpers.
finding.source: req.params.id from the URL, sent by any authenticated user (or by an unauthenticated caller if no upstream middleware sets req.user) who does not own the project

trace.note: project is loaded by the request-supplied id with no ownership check
authorized(req.user, project) returns false for a non-owner, but the return value is discarded with no if, return or throw
authorized() only returns a boolean and never throws

finding.guards_checked: Only api.js exists in the directory, so I could not read any upstream auth middleware. The in-handler check is the only one visible, and its result is not enforced. The PUT route's authorize() does throw, so it is not affected. Missing project: store.get may return undefined, which would cause a TypeError (a 500, not a security issue).

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean and never throws; its result is discarded at api.js:18. No other control is visible in api.js, and no upstream middleware exists in the directory. The PUT route's authorize() (api.js:4-10) throws and is correct.
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls the boolean-returning authorized() as a bare statement, so api.js:19 deletes the project for any caller (non-owner included) who reaches the route. Every trace line matches. The finding's own caveat holds: an upstream auth middleware could not be checked, so the attacker may need to be authenticated.
